newsitem.title: USA: Caribbean region warned to watch new storm system.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean region warned to watch new storm system.

text.p: A tropical depression developed Tuesday in the western Caribbean and was expected to strengthen as it moved toward Cuba, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the center of tropical depression 12 was near latitude 16.1 north and longitude 83.0 west, or about 110 miles (175 km) south-southeast of Swan Island, and about 490 miles (790 km) south of Havana.

The depression was moving northwest at a rate of about 10 mph (16 kph), and this was expected to continue through Tuesday night. Maximum sustained winds were near 35 mph (55 kph) and the depression was likely to strengthen to a tropical storm later on Tuesday.

"We're forecasting intensification. At this point we think it will be a tropical storm later today (Tuesday)," said National Hurricane Center forecaster Ed Rappaport. "It's possible it will reach hurricane strength by the time it gets to Cuba."

The hurricane center warned all interests in the northwestern Caribbean, Cuba, the eastern Gulf of Mexico, and Florida to monitor the storm closely and said a hurricane watch could be issued for western Cuba as early as Tuesday afternoon.
The depression would become Tropical Storm Lili if maximum sustained winds reached 39 mph (62 kph). It would become a hurricane if such winds reached 74 mph (119 kph).
The system was expected to shift from its northwestern track to a more northerly and then northeasterly direction during the next three days.
